# The digraph a unit prints names the program's functions the way the
# runtime does, so it composes with the call graph of the program itself.
# golang.org/x/tools/cmd/callgraph names a function by its package path,
# which for a main package is the import path rather than "main", so one
# rename joins the two graphs. The composed graph then answers a question
# neither half can: which path through the program's code reaches the
# division slowpath in the compiled kernel.
#
# The program below has the call shape of the one the fused_layered fixture
# was compiled from: fastMath reaches the kernel only through attribute,
# which the unit records as the caller of layered.
[!exec:callgraph] skip
[!exec:digraph] skip
[!exec:sh] skip
[short] skip
exec sh -c 'cd $WORK/wiring && callgraph -algo=static -format=digraph . | sed "s|example.com/wiring\.|main.|g" > $WORK/all.txt && cudalineinfo -sass $TESTDATA/fused_layered.sass -ptx $TESTDATA/fused_layered.ptx -format digraph $TESTDATA/fused_layered.json >> $WORK/all.txt && digraph somepath main.fastMath "$(digraph nodes < $WORK/all.txt | grep div_rn_noftz_f32_slowpath)" < $WORK/all.txt'
stdout 'main.fastMath main.attribute'
stdout 'main.attribute main.layered'
stdout '\$__internal_[0-9]+_\$__cuda_sm3x_div_rn_noftz_f32_slowpath'

-- wiring/go.mod --
module example.com/wiring

go 1.22
-- wiring/main.go --
package main

type kernel struct {
	name  string
	build func()
}

func main() { fastMath() }

func fastMath() { attribute(kernel{"fused_layered", layered}) }

func attribute(k kernel) { k.build() }

func layered() {}
